title: 3.5.18 Lab: Rewrite a Multi-Parameter Function to Take an Object
description: Take a function with three positional parameters and rewrite it to read one options object instead. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write the positional original
steps.instructions: Write a function called describeBox that takes three positional parameters (width, height and color) and returns a string built from them.

steps.title: Rewrite it to take one object
steps.instructions: Change describeBox so it takes a single parameter, an options object, and reads width, height and color off that object with a dot.

steps.title: Call it with an options object
steps.instructions: Call describeBox with one object literal that names the three keys, and print the result.

requirements.title: function defined
requirements.description: Defines a function. Help: 3.5.16 (Objects as Named Arguments)
requirements.hint: Define the function with the function keyword and a name of your choice.

requirements.title: reads a property off the options object
requirements.description: Uses options.property in the body. Help: 3.5.16 (Objects as Named Arguments)
requirements.hint: The single parameter is the options object. Read each value off it with a dot, like options.width.

requirements.title: called with an object literal
requirements.description: A call passes a brace literal. Help: 3.5.16 (Objects as Named Arguments)
requirements.hint: Call the function with one object in braces that names each key, such as { width: 10, height: 4 }.

requirements.title: result printed
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.5.16 (Objects as Named Arguments)
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: describeBox takes one options object and uses all three values
requirements.description: describeBox({ width: 2, height: 3, color: "red" }) returns text containing red, 2 and 3, a second object gives its own values, and the function takes exactly one parameter. Help: 3.5.17 (Example: An Options Object)
requirements.hint: describeBox should have ONE parameter, the options object. Read options.width, options.height and options.color, and put all three in the string it returns.

checks.expr: typeof describeBox === 'function' && describeBox.length === 1 && (s => s.includes('red') && s.includes('2') && s.includes('3'))(String(describeBox({ width: 2, height: 3, color: 'red' }))) && (s => s.includes('blue') && s.includes('7') && s.includes('9'))(String(describeBox({ color: 'blue', height: 9, width: 7 })))
checks.fail: describeBox should take one options object and use all three values: describeBox({ width: 2, height: 3, color: "red" }) must give text that contains red, 2 and 3.
